---
title: Batch inference
description: "Score large request files to Parquet shards without holding every prediction in memory."
---

Supply your application's Parquet request files through `ArrowDataModule`.
Use Lightning prediction with `rf.Writer` to write results directly to Parquet,
keeping large jobs from accumulating every prediction in memory.

The example uses the transaction-history model trained in
[Train and save](../learn/train-and-save.qmd). Each request row keeps its
`trxns` inputs and omits `disputed`, as shown in
[Prediction output](../reference/prediction-output.qmd). The model returns a dispute result
for every retained transaction.

```python
import relflow as rf

# The application supplies the request files for the trained model.
data = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    predict="payments/history/scoring/*.parquet",
    retain=("payment_id",),
)
model.predict(
    datamodule=data,
    batch_size=256,
    callbacks=[rf.Writer("payment-predictions")],
    return_predictions=False,
)
```

Each rank writes `payment-predictions/rank-{global_rank}.parquet`. With
[prediction output](../reference/prediction-output.qmd), these files preserve the
selected `predictions`, `representations`, and retained `inputs` columns and
schema metadata. Repeated records are variable lists of sibling result structs,
even with finite branch limits. Retain a business key to join or sort distributed
results downstream; relflow does not add row identity.

Use a new output directory for each job. A Writer replaces its own rank's shard;
it does not remove shards left by another job with a different rank count. Read
the output only after prediction finishes successfully. During a run, shards
have a `.partial` suffix and receive their final names at completion.

To collect bounded batched output in memory, use
`model.predict(datamodule=data, batch_size=256, devices=1)`. This returns one Polars DataFrame.
The batch size is per device and updates the model's current size.
Prediction has no automatic time limit.

With `drop_last=False` (the default), distributed prediction preserves the final
partial group. Ranks receive disjoint rows; a short tail can leave some ranks
with no rows in that step. Local prediction workers take turns on complete rank
batches, preserving their order within each rank's shard. Combining shards does
not restore global source order. Use retained identifiers to join or sort the
results, or use one device when source order is needed without that step.

As an alternative, a [postprocessor](postprocessing.qmd) can give files a
consumer-specific schema. Configure a different Writer:

```python
writer = rf.Writer("warehouse-predictions", postprocessor=warehouse)
```

Here `warehouse` is an application-defined decorated processor. The first
written batch fixes that rank's Parquet schema; later batches must match it.
Pass this `writer` in `callbacks=[writer]` instead of the original Writer to
produce `warehouse-predictions/`. Processors may change rows and columns for
offline output.

For the original job above, scan its completed shards with Polars. Select and
filter the needed results before collecting an in-memory DataFrame:

```python
import polars as pl

results = pl.scan_parquet("payment-predictions/rank-*.parquet")
payment_ids = results.select(
    payment_id=pl.col("inputs").struct.field("payment_id"),
).collect()
```

## Fixed-size vectors and null containers

When writing Parquet, `rf.Writer` rejects a fixed-size list beneath a null ancestor or a null vector
value because PyArrow 24 cannot round-trip that shape through Parquet. A Vector
field in a structurally null repeated record can trigger this guard, as can a
retained source vector. Null components inside a nonnull fixed-size vector are
different and remain supported. The guard runs after configured postprocessing.

Use streaming Arrow IPC for affected results to preserve their vector widths
and nulls without collecting the entire job:

```python
model.predict(
    datamodule=data,
    batch_size=256,
    devices=1,
    callbacks=[rf.Writer("payment-predictions-ipc", format="ipc")],
    return_predictions=False,
)
```

IPC shards use `rank-N.arrow` and the Arrow IPC file format, readable by
Polars, PyArrow, and `rf.source(...)`. Both formats retain schema metadata,
buffer batches into bounded groups, and publish their final filenames only
after prediction ends successfully. The [CLI](command-line.qmd) exposes the
same choice through `relflow predict ... --format ipc`.

Direct prediction also supports bounded in-memory requests, processing rows in
batches and collecting one Polars DataFrame.
[Prediction output](../reference/prediction-output.qmd#batch-direct-requests) explains its
preprocessing and postprocessing order. Data-module prediction with a Writer
streams file-backed datasets. Use [Serving](serving.qmd) for online requests.
